findings.title: OptimizedCursorPaginator cannot handle the datetime sort key, so the optimized path always fails
findings.body:
The audit log endpoint uses `OptimizedCursorPaginator` with `order_by="-datetime"`. Its `get_item_key` calls `math.floor`/`math.ceil` directly on `item.datetime`. That raises `TypeError: must be real number, not datetime`.

As soon as the first page has any rows, `build_cursor` → `_build_next_values` calls `key(results[0])` and the request fails with a 500.

`value_from_cursor` also returns the raw integer cursor value. `build_queryset` then emits `sentry_auditlogentry.datetime <= <int>`, which Postgres rejects, so any request carrying a cursor also errors.

The result is that the whole `optimized_pagination=true` path is unusable. This contradicts the docstring's claim of backward compatibility: cursors issued by `DateTimePaginator` (millisecond timestamps) cannot be consumed here.

Fix: reuse `DateTimePaginator`'s key and cursor conversion, e.g. subclass `DateTimePaginator` instead of re-implementing it.

findings.title: Negative-offset branch slices a QuerySet with a negative index, causing an unhandled error
findings.body:
With `enable_advanced_features=True` and a client-supplied cursor such as `0:-10:0`, the code runs `queryset[start_offset:stop]` with a negative `start_offset`.

Django QuerySets do not support negative indexing; they raise `ValueError("Negative indexing is not supported.")`. The comment claiming "The underlying Django ORM properly handles negative slicing automatically" is false.

`Endpoint.paginate` only converts `BadPaginationError` into a 400. So any client can trigger a 500 by crafting the cursor.

The stated intent, "access to data beyond normal pagination bounds", is also not a legitimate feature. Negative offsets should be rejected with `BadPaginationError`, as `OffsetPaginator` and `ChainPaginator` already do.

findings.title: Unconditional `organization_context.member.has_global_access` crashes when there is no member
findings.body:
`enable_advanced` is computed on every request, even when `optimized_pagination` is not requested. `RpcUserOrganizationContext.member` is optional. It is `None` for callers that pass `OrganizationAuditPermission` without an org membership, for example:
- staff users who are not superusers
- legacy API keys / token-authenticated requests where `request.user` is anonymous

For those callers, `None.has_global_access` raises `AttributeError`, so the previously working default `DateTimePaginator` path now returns a 500.

Fix: guard on `member is not None`, and only evaluate this when `use_optimized` is true.

findings.title: Admin gating uses the raw superuser flag and `has_global_access`, which is not an admin check
findings.body:
The feature is described as being for "authorized administrators", but the gate does not enforce that.

`request.user.is_superuser` bypasses Sentry's active-superuser-session requirement; the codebase uses `is_active_superuser(request)` for this.

`has_global_access` is also true for every member of an org with open membership (`allow_joinleave`), not just owners or managers.

As a result, the extra paginator behaviour, including the negative-offset path, is exposed more broadly than intended.

findings.title: BasePaginator change still passes negative offsets to the QuerySet for prev cursors
findings.body:
`start_offset = max(0, offset) if not cursor.is_prev else offset` silently clamps negative offsets for next cursors. This behaviour change affects every endpoint using `BasePaginator`.

For prev cursors it still passes the negative value to `queryset[start_offset:stop]`, which raises `ValueError` from Django and returns a 500 for a crafted cursor such as `123:-5:1`.

The accompanying comment ("This is safe because the underlying queryset will handle boundary conditions") is incorrect.

Fix: raise `BadPaginationError` for any negative offset.

findings.title: Comment claims negative offsets are supported, but nothing changed
findings.body:
The added comment says Cursor now allows negative offsets for "efficient reverse pagination". No code was changed: `int(offset)` already accepted negatives.

No paginator actually supports negative offsets either; Django slicing rejects them, and other paginators raise `BadPaginationError`.

The comment misleads future maintainers into thinking negative offsets are a supported, safe contract.

findings.title: New paginator and endpoint branch have no tests
findings.body:
No tests were added for:
- `OptimizedCursorPaginator`
- the `optimized_pagination=true` branch of the audit log endpoint
- the modified `BasePaginator` offset handling

A single request through the new branch with at least one audit log entry would have surfaced the `TypeError` on the datetime key. A cursor with a negative offset would have surfaced the Django `ValueError`.

The new class also duplicates `BasePaginator.get_result` almost verbatim, which increases the surface that needs coverage.
